framework: ABC: Agentic Benchmark Checklist (Zhu et al., NeurIPS 2025)
rule: items mapped to C05, C07, C12, C14, or C28

items.text: Versions of all tools (e.g., Python) are clearly specified.
All required API tools are consistently accessible to agents during evaluation.
Evaluation process terminates or handles errors appropriately if an API becomes inaccessible.
Residual data or state are fully cleared between runs.
Agent is completely isolated from any ground truth information.
The environment setup is fully reproducible and frozen at the time of benchmark release, without reliance on dynamic external resources.
Annotated ground truth is verified for correctness.
Each task is verified to be solvable.
Benchmark includes an Oracle solver that can automatically solve all challenges.
Outliers in pilot experiments are inspected to identify implementation bugs, impossible tasks or shortcuts.
Considers expressions semantically equivalent to ground truth.
Handles redundant words used by agents.
Handles negation modifiers used by agents.
Is robust against systematically listing all possible answers.
Ground truth is sufficiently complex to prevent guessing.
Demonstrates documented or experimental evidence of the judge's accuracy, self-consistency, and agreement with human.
Is designed to resist adversarial inputs and reward hacking.
Verifies test cases for correctness and quality (e.g., by human).
Measures quality of test cases using objective metrics (e.g., code coverage, cyclomatic complexity control).
Addresses potential edge cases.
Ensures comprehensive coverage of all relevant input variations (e.g., data types, memory layouts, value ranges).
Generates inputs that the code under testing is sensitive to.
Covers all possible branches of user workflows.
Exercises all relevant parts of the code being tested.
Prevents non-deterministic ("flaky") test results.
Ground truth includes all states achievable after success.
Checks relevant and irrelevant states for the challenge.
Ground truth is complex to prevent trivial state modifications.
Designs quality metrics that prevent exploitation (e.g., achieving high scores by reward hacking)
Includes measures to prevent data contamination, such as a private, held-out test set, or a lively updated dataset.
Includes measures or plans to consistently update challenges over time to avoid overfitting.
Includes quantitative analysis to assess the impact of unavoidable flaws (e.g., noise of ground truth).
Reports metrics about statistical significance, such as confidence intervals.
